output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, the acquisition is completed, but its litigation legacy remains unresolved: Bayer’s November 3 disclosure described a proposed Roundup class settlement of up to US$7.25 billion over up to 21 years that was not yet final. Bayer became Monsanto’s sole owner on June 7, 2018, paying US$128 per share in cash; its June 4, 2018 pre-closing estimate put the total acquisition cost at approximately US$63 billion, including Monsanto’s outstanding debt. The merger agreement was announced on September 14, 2016, with the strategic aim of combining Monsanto’s seeds, traits and digital agriculture capabilities with Bayer’s crop-protection business. Antitrust clearance required divestitures to BASF—including seed businesses and Liberty herbicide—which the U.S. Justice Department valued at approximately US$9 billion in May 2018. Bayer said it would discontinue the Monsanto company name while retaining the acquired products’ brand names.
caveats: The approximately US$63 billion figure was Bayer’s June 4, 2018 estimate using Monsanto’s debt outstanding as of February 28, 2018—not a current valuation.

The litigation status reflects Bayer’s November 3, 2026 disclosure: the class settlement had preliminary approval, but final approval and completion of any appeals remained conditions to effectiveness; subsequent court action may change that status.

key_facts.fact: Bayer disclosed proposed Monsanto Roundup class-settlement payments totaling up to US$7.25 billion over up to 21 years. The settlement was not yet final and effective.
Bayer completed the acquisition, became Monsanto’s sole owner, and paid shareholders US$128 per share.
Bayer and Monsanto announced a signed definitive merger agreement for an all-cash acquisition at US$128 per share.
Bayer estimated the total acquisition cost at approximately US$63 billion, including Monsanto’s debt outstanding as of February 28, 2018.
The U.S. Justice Department required approximately US$9 billion in divestitures to BASF, including Bayer’s cotton, canola, soybean and vegetable seed businesses and Liberty herbicide business.
The stated strategic rationale was to combine Monsanto’s seeds, traits and digital agriculture capabilities with Bayer’s crop-protection products.
Bayer announced that the Monsanto company name would be discontinued, while acquired products would retain their brand names.
